Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In a directed graph stored with an adjacency list, the cost of the operation for vertex v equals the number of outgoing edges from v, which is simply the length of v's adjacency list. The worst-case single operation occurs when a vertex points to every other vertex in the graph, and the average amortized cost is derived by summing all operation costs and dividing by the total number of operations.

* **(a) Worst-case single operation:** The maximum number of outgoing edges a single vertex can have in a simple directed graph with |V| vertices is **|V| − 1**, so the worst possible cost of one operation is |V| − 1.

* **(b) Average amortized cost (aggregate analysis):** The total cost of the entire sequence of |V| operations is the sum of the out-degrees of all vertices, which equals the total number of edges |E|. Dividing this total by the number of operations (|V|) gives an average amortized cost of **|E| / |V|**.
